reviews.title: Exceptional Cooling Performance with Stunning ARGB Lighting
reviews.comment:
I've been using the AsiaHorse WK-A360 ARGB All-in-One AIO CPU Liquid Cooler for several weeks, and it has exceeded my expectations in both performance and aesthetics.
Cooling Efficiency:
The dual high-performance pumps, operating at 3000 RPM and 4500 RPM, ensure optimal coolant flow, effectively keeping my CPU temperatures low even during intensive tasks. The 360mm radiator, combined with three 120mm PWM fans, provides excellent heat dissipation, maintaining system stability under heavy loads.
ASIAHORSE-PC
Design and Aesthetics:
The ARGB lighting is vibrant and customizable, seamlessly syncing with my motherboard's RGB software. The 360° rotatable pump top, featuring the unique AsiaHorse logo, adds a sleek and modern touch to my build. The white color variant complements my setup perfectly, enhancing the overall visual appeal.
ASIAHORSE-PC
Installation and Compatibility:
Installation was straightforward, thanks to the clear instructions and included mounting hardware compatible with both Intel and AMD sockets. The 400mm tubing length provided ample flexibility for routing within my mid-tower case.
ASIAHORSE-PC
Pros:
Superior Cooling Performance: Effectively manages high CPU loads, keeping temperatures in check.
Aesthetic Appeal: Vibrant ARGB lighting and sleek design enhance the build's look.
Quiet Operation: Fans operate quietly, even at higher speeds, maintaining a peaceful environment.
Easy Installation: Compatible with a wide range of Intel and AMD sockets, with clear installation instructions.
Cons:
Software Integration: While the ARGB lighting syncs well with major motherboard software, additional customization options within a dedicated AsiaHorse software would be a welcome enhancement.
Final Thoughts:
The AsiaHorse WK-A360 ARGB AIO CPU Liquid Cooler offers exceptional cooling performance coupled with stunning aesthetics. It's an excellent choice for gamers and PC enthusiasts seeking both functionality and style in their cooling solutions. I highly recommend this cooler for its performance, design, and value.
For more information and to purchase, you can visit the product page on Amazon: AsiaHorse WK-A360 ARGB All-in-One AIO CPU Liquid Cooler

reviews.title: Priceworthy
reviews.comment:
Never been a big fan (no pun intended) of "liquid coolers" because they were always pricey for what they offered and most of the time you can keep your CPU cool with a good fan.
So when I saw this cooler offered at the $100.00 mark and the decent reviews given, I thought I'd give it a try. I removed a noctua cpu cooler that was MASSIVE in size and sounded like an A-10 Thunderbolt coming in for a run....but, it did keep my AMD Ryzen 9 7950X3D right at it's performance level.
As far as the install goes? It was kinda cumbersome hooking  all the fans, radiator and cpu cooler together but that was to be expected. I would caution you to make sure you have the footprint allowable in your case for this cooler. I have a full tower and that allowed the right amount of maneuverability for all the wiring, fans at the top and the bend for the hoses.
The performance was adequate. (see idle and full speed pictures) I saw absolutely no difference in cooling but to be honest I didn't expect to (see temp pics). I ran COD 7 at full detail (4K) and settings about as high as they could go (see pic) just to make sure I heated the processor up under the AsiaHorse. This would give me a look at it's full potential to keep the CPU cool. The AsiaHorse performed fine. The noctua cpu cooler I was running previously had two upright embedded fans and 8 pipes to absorb the heat. However the footprint reduction with the AsiaHorse CPU Liquid Cooler was PERFECT for my Full Tower (see pic). The AsiaHorse Cooler is also much quieter then the Noctua Fan I had. With the AsiaHorse Cooler I stayed well under the TJMax temp of the CPU and again it performed well.  So no complaints on performance.
A few things to take into account: Make sure you have the room in your Tower, (2) 3pin ARGB connections on your mother board and a couple (3) 4pin fan connections.
Bottom line? It's a fairly decent cooler if you're looking to keep a low profile, decent noise level and keep your CPU cool. I would also suggest that you reach out to the distributor/manufacturer and make sure it supports your processor.
Overall it's a decent buy for its performance.
